title: A live herdr can never deliver the gate's unexpected_answer finding
description:
The gate hands its confirm wait the same budget twice: waitCtx and params.Timeout are both ConfirmTimeout (gate.go:131 and :136). herdr starts its own identical budget only once it has received the request, so its CodeTimeout answer always arrives after the caller's context deadline has already fired, and the client returns its own i/o timeout first. A confirm-budget expiry against a live herdr therefore never observes herdr's reported timeout: the gate records GateUnconfirmed with a client-side read-timeout observation, and GateUnexpectedAnswer — documented as the finding for 'the prompt was observed to land and no working was observed within the budget' — is unreachable through the live protocol; only a herdr that answers a timeout early (never, for a live one) or a test that replaces the route can produce it. Nothing consumes DispatchGate mechanically, so the cost is observability: a landed prompt with a silent agent is recorded as 'could observe neither' instead of 'not the expected work'. This tick's fixture change makes the test fake answer early, so the suite now exercises unexpected_answer; production herdr still always loses the race.
evidence: internal/exec/herdr/gate.go:131 and :136 give the caller's ctx and herdr's own wait the same ConfirmTimeout; the red-test run at base recorded 'the confirmation wait answered herd/client: reading agent.wait response: ... i/o timeout' while the fake's identical-deadline answer was still pending (1.007007708s burn of the 1s budget)
